prs.title: fix: buffer stdio server writes during progress notifications
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both address stdio write-stream blocking caused by the memory object stream being an unbuffered (buffer size 0) rendezvous channel: a handler trying to queue its final response can block while the stdout writer task is still flushing an earlier message (e.g. a progress notification). #2215 exposes read_stream_buffer_size/write_stream_buffer_size as caller-supplied parameters (defaulting to 0, i.e. unchanged behavior unless a caller opts in). #2654 hardcodes the write_stream buffer to 1 directly in stdio_server, fixing the blocking behavior out of the box. Both PRs modify the exact same memory-object-stream construction lines in stdio_server and would conflict on merge. (2 PRs)

clusters.pick_reason: 3012 factors the fix into a standalone _iter_www_auth_params tokenizer that tracks an escape_next state, so a quoted value containing a backslash-escaped quote (\") is parsed correctly per RFC 7235 quoted-string grammar. 3016's inline scanner only toggles in_quotes on every literal '"' with no escape handling, so a value containing an escaped quote would flip the parser out of the quoted range prematurely and mis-split the header. 3012's extraction into a named, independently testable helper is also easier to unit test in isolation.

members.author: tarunag10
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py::extract_field_from_www_auth used a single regex search (field_name=(?:"([^"]+)"|([^\s,]+))) over the raw WWW-Authenticate header, which can match a field name/value that appears inside another parameter's quoted value or otherwise fails to respect auth-param boundaries. Both PRs replace this with a proper comma-separated, quote-aware parameter scan. clusters.pick_reason: #2654 fixes the blocking-during-progress-notifications problem by default (buffer=1) with no API changes required from callers, and ships a targeted regression test (BlockingStdout) that reproduces the exact race being fixed. #2215's fix only takes effect if a caller explicitly passes write_stream_buffer_size=1, so it doesn't resolve the reported issue for existing callers using stdio_server's default construction. #2215's diff is also based on the older `anyio.create_memory_object_stream` call sites rather than the `create_context_streams` helper already in use by #2552/#2654/#2766, so it is stale relative to the current stdio.py and would need a rebase with conflicts on these same lines.

members.title: fix(stdio): allow configurable memory stream buffer size
members.author: yaowubarbara
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2654: Both address stdio write-stream blocking caused by the memory object stream being an unbuffered (buffer size 0) rendezvous channel: a handler trying to queue its final response can block while the stdout writer task is still flushing an earlier message (e.g. a progress notification). #2215 exposes read_stream_buffer_size/write_stream_buffer_size as caller-supplied parameters (defaulting to 0, i.e. unchanged behavior unless a caller opts in). #2654 hardcodes the write_stream buffer to 1 directly in stdio_server, fixing the blocking behavior out of the box. Both PRs modify the exact same memory-object-stream construction lines in stdio_server and would conflict on merge.

clusters.pick_reason: 3012 factors the fix into a standalone _iter_www_auth_params tokenizer that tracks an escape_next state, so a quoted value containing a backslash-escaped quote (\") is parsed correctly per RFC 7235 quoted-string grammar. 3016's inline scanner only toggles in_quotes on every literal '"' with no escape handling, so a value containing an escaped quote would flip the parser out of the quoted range prematurely and mis-split the header. 3012's extraction into a named, independently testable helper is also easier to unit test in isolation.

members.title: fix(auth): match complete WWW-Authenticate parameters
members.author: tarunag10
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py::extract_field_from_www_auth used a single regex search (field_name=(?:"([^"]+)"|([^\s,]+))) over the raw WWW-Authenticate header, which can match a field name/value that appears inside another parameter's quoted value or otherwise fails to respect auth-param boundaries. Both PRs replace this with a proper comma-separated, quote-aware parameter scan. Both branch from the identical base commit (d6b05e066), confirming independent parallel fixes of the same bug rather than sequential work. (2 PRs)
